name: Jezero Crater rim
geologicalDescription: Impact crater rim; use USGS crater-rim crest lines and rim-unit polygons, not a point.
scientificSignificance: Defines basin boundary and relief; rim breaching records past hydrology.
coordinateSource: Existing clipped SIM 3464 line and polygon layers; this register does not duplicate geometry.

name: Western Delta
geologicalDescription: Western fluvio-deltaic fan deposits at the mouth of Neretva Vallis.
scientificSignificance: Preserves fluvial and lacustrine deposits and potential biosignature-bearing sediments.
perseveranceHistory: Perseverance explored the western fan and sampled its sedimentary succession.
coordinateSource: Mapped extent should be joined from a source geologic polygon; no centroid substituted.

name: Northern Delta
geologicalDescription: Eroded fan deposits in the northern crater; literature notes their origin and relation to the western delta remain debated.
scientificSignificance: Constrains northern-inlet sediment transport and basin history.
coordinateSource: Use mapped deposits and preserve interpretation caveat; no point coordinate assigned.

name: Neretva Vallis
geometryType: LineString region; point is official center
geometryNote: Geometry is the official gazetteer center point for catalog display; the named landform is linear and its source extent is recorded separately.
geologicalDescription: Inlet valley/channel entering Jezero from the west/northwest.
scientificSignificance: Records fluvial transport into the paleolake; rover observations include fluvio-lacustrine strata.
perseveranceHistory: Perseverance investigated the inlet channel including Tuff Cliff / Bright Angel region.
coordinateSource: Representative point is the Gazetteer center (77.20°E, 18.55°N); source extent 77.00–77.30°E, 18.50–18.60°N. Full feature remains linear.

name: Sava Vallis
geometryType: LineString region; point is official center
geometryNote: Geometry is the official gazetteer center point for catalog display; the named landform is linear and its source extent is recorded separately.
geologicalDescription: Named western/northern inlet valley system in regional nomenclature.
scientificSignificance: Evidence for fluvial inflow to Jezero basin.
coordinateSource: Representative point is the Gazetteer center (77.13°E, 19.09°N); source extent 76.69–77.56°E, 18.74–19.43°N, so the valley crosses the DEM boundary.

name: Eastern Outlet Valley (Pliva Vallis)
geometryType: LineString region; point is official center
geometryNote: Geometry is the official gazetteer center point for catalog display; the named landform is linear and its source extent is recorded separately.
geologicalDescription: The eastern outlet channel is officially named Pliva Vallis; “Eastern Outlet Valley” is a descriptive synonym, not a separate feature.
scientificSignificance: Records overflow/drainage and episodic fluvial activity.
coordinateSource: Representative point is the Gazetteer center (78.35°E, 18.67°N); source extent 78.09–78.60°E, 18.52–18.81°N, extending slightly beyond the DEM east edge.

name: Ancient lake basin
geologicalDescription: Jezero hosted an ancient lake; reconstructed lake extents vary with inferred water level and time.
scientificSignificance: Habitability context and depositional setting for delta/lacustrine sediments.
perseveranceHistory: Mission investigates rocks formed in and around the paleolake.
coordinateSource: Represent individual published paleolake-level contours as separate dated/inferred lines; no single exact polygon asserted.

name: Crater rim breach
geologicalDescription: Eroded eastern rim breach/outlet associated with discharge through Pliva Vallis.
scientificSignificance: Constrains open-basin phase and outflow-flood history.
sourceName: Fassett et al. outlet-forming flood study
coordinateSource: Requires DEM-derived/local mapped breach outline; not a point.

name: Kodiak Butte (Kodiak)
geometryType: Point plus mapped polygon if sourced
geologicalDescription: Eroded isolated western fan remnant with preserved bottomset, foreset, and topset strata.
scientificSignificance: Key evidence for Jezero delta deposition and changing lake level.
perseveranceHistory: Imaged by Perseverance from the landing region; not a rover stop named as the feature center.
coordinateSource: Published orbital/rover mapping identifies it; this repo has no verified footprint/center coordinate. No screenshot estimate.

name: Octavia E. Butler Landing Site
geologicalDescription: Perseverance touchdown location.
scientificSignificance: Mission entry point for in-situ exploration.
perseveranceHistory: Touchdown on Sol 0, 18 February 2021.
coordinateSource: Published landing coordinate 77.4509°E, 18.4446°N; planetocentric, east-positive.

name: Séítah
geologicalDescription: Informal name for olivine-rich crater-floor unit and rover exploration area; consists of dispersed exposures among aeolian bedforms.
scientificSignificance: Records ancient igneous/crater-floor geology, with possible aqueous alteration.
perseveranceHistory: Explored during first science campaign; rover traversed exposures and collected samples.
coordinateSource: Use mapped unit/exposure geometry; avoid a single point for broad unit.

name: Máaz Formation
geologicalDescription: Informal name for basaltic crater-floor rocks overlying Séítah.
scientificSignificance: Constrains igneous history and the stratigraphy of Jezero floor.
perseveranceHistory: Studied and sampled during first science campaign.
coordinateSource: Use published unit map/USGS correlations, not point coordinate.

name: Three Forks
geologicalDescription: Named location of Perseverance's sample depot. Depot event table identifies ten drops but does not provide individual tube coordinates.
scientificSignificance: Preserves cached samples for possible future return.
perseveranceHistory: Ten sample tubes deposited during December 2022–January 2023; individual positions must not be inferred from rover position.
sourceName: NASA annotated panorama; PDS Three Forks depot bundle
coordinateSource: Exact depot coordinate / individual tube locations not joined in repository.

name: Hawksbill Gap
geologicalDescription: Named passage/outcrop area in the western delta front, associated with the Shenandoah formation.
scientificSignificance: Exposes delta-front sedimentary stratigraphy.
perseveranceHistory: Perseverance traversed and sampled in the delta-front campaign.
sourceName: NASA annotated panorama; AGU stratigraphy paper
coordinateSource: Use rover observation localizations or source map GIS; no point inferred from illustration.

name: Kodiak
geologicalDescription: Same geological landmark as Kodiak Butte; not a second feature.
scientificSignificance: Delta stratigraphy and paleolake-level evidence.
perseveranceHistory: Perseverance observed remotely; distinguish rover observation positions from butte location.
coordinateSource: Alias of Kodiak Butte; deduplicate geometry.

name: Belva Crater
geologicalDescription: Named impact crater and nearby rover observation area. Existing “Belva” coordinate is a USGS text-label anchor, not necessarily crater center.
scientificSignificance: Provides exposure/context for crater-floor stratigraphy.
perseveranceHistory: Visited/imaged by Perseverance during delta approach.
coordinateSource: Existing anchor in jezero_landmarks.geojson must not be promoted to crater center.

name: Enchanted Lake
geologicalDescription: Informal rover-era name; precise feature footprint and authoritative coordinate are not present in bundled sources.
scientificSignificance: Not assigned beyond mission waypoint context until primary mission reference is linked.
perseveranceHistory: Not independently verified in currently bundled primary sources.
coordinateSource: Do not place until map waypoint feature data is obtained.

name: Cape Nukshak
geologicalDescription: Named section/outcrop along eastern scarp of the western delta, in the Shenandoah formation.
scientificSignificance: Exposes lower delta sequence and facies architecture.
perseveranceHistory: Perseverance investigated the section during delta-front campaign.
sourceName: NASA NTRS lower delta sequence study
coordinateSource: Source confirms location context; exact geometry needs mission waypoint join.

name: Artuby Ridge
geologicalDescription: Informal ridge/region south of landing area, associated with Máaz/Séítah exposures.
scientificSignificance: Stratigraphic relationships and crater-floor geology.
perseveranceHistory: Perseverance traversed and investigated Artuby Ridge; flight reconnaissance supported planning.
coordinateSource: Use source map / PLACES localized stops to trace rover traverse; no representative point inferred.

name: Tuff Cliff
geologicalDescription: Outcrop/member in Neretva Vallis inlet channel, stratigraphically associated with fluvio-lacustrine deposits.
scientificSignificance: Records transition toward sustained lacustrine conditions.
perseveranceHistory: Observed by Perseverance in the Bright Angel exploration region.
coordinateSource: Precise feature geometry not bundled; NASA panorama says outcrop is ~480 m east of Cheyava Falls but that is not a coordinate.

name: Valinor Hills
geologicalDescription: Informal named feature appearing on NASA Mars 2020 traverse map materials.
scientificSignificance: No independent scientific interpretation assigned from available source.
perseveranceHistory: Mission traverse-map label; exact footprint not joined.
coordinateSource: NASA figure label is not coordinate geometry.

name: Beehive Geyser
geologicalDescription: Informal area about 500 m west of the rover at Sol 1059; name does not establish a geological geyser process.
scientificSignificance: NASA describes a margin-unit interval about 60 m above an earlier sampled section; scientific interest is stratigraphic comparison.
perseveranceHistory: Perseverance planned an excursion there in February 2024.
coordinateSource: Relative distance/direction only; do not turn into a coordinate.

name: Bunsen Peak
geologicalDescription: Large rock on a ridge in the Margin unit; sample source for Comet Geyser.
scientificSignificance: Sampled sedimentary rock helps characterize the carbonate-bearing Margin unit.
perseveranceHistory: Perseverance performed proximity science and collected its 27th named sample at the Bunsen Peak target on Sol 1088.
sourceName: NASA Science and NASA sample inventory
coordinateSource: Named target confirmed; exact location can be joined from rover localization and sample event metadata.

name: Jurabi Point
geologicalDescription: Named waypoint in the Margin Unit campaign.
scientificSignificance: Provides context for the rover's exploration of carbonate-bearing margin terrain.
perseveranceHistory: Perseverance passed through Jurabi Point during the 2024 Margin Unit traverse.
sourceName: NASA Science, New Year, New Images from Mars
coordinateSource: Waypoint location needs rover localization join.

name: Gnaraloo Bay
geologicalDescription: Erosional window through the western fan apex exposing underlying Margin Unit.
scientificSignificance: Exposes the fan-Margin unconformity and stratigraphic relations.
perseveranceHistory: Perseverance explored the region approximately Sols 952–999.
coordinateSource: Published regional description; exact boundary should be digitized from source map, not approximated.

name: Mandu Wall
geologicalDescription: Named Margin Unit terrain region associated with the first sample, Pelican Point.
scientificSignificance: Context for carbonate-bearing rocks and possible shoreline/volcanic/alteration interpretations.
perseveranceHistory: Explored during the Margin campaign; Pelican Point collected from workspace within Mandu Wall.
coordinateSource: Use traverse/sample observations and regional mapping; no representative point asserted.

name: Pelican Point
geologicalDescription: Perseverance sample name collected at Hans Amundsen Memorial Workspace within Mandu Wall.
scientificSignificance: First sample from the carbonate-rich Margin Unit; helps assess its origin and habitability context.
perseveranceHistory: Core/sample 22 collected on Sol 923.
coordinateSource: Sample/workspace coordinates should be joined from PDS PLACES or sample localization metadata.

name: Pinestand
geologicalDescription: Requested name not verified in available bundled authoritative sources; do not assume it is a distinct Jezero landmark.
scientificSignificance: Unassigned pending verification.
perseveranceHistory: No verified exploration record in sources reviewed.
coordinateSource: Name and coordinate need primary source confirmation.

name: Faraway Rock
geologicalDescription: Named group of rocks near the inner crater rim, encountered at the start of the crater-rim campaign.
scientificSignificance: Rim campaign explores older crustal materials and stratigraphy.
perseveranceHistory: Perseverance reached the area around Sol 1282 and began the rim ascent campaign.
coordinateSource: Named regional location confirmed; rover stop/localization join required for coordinate.
